$comment: Cross-runtime golden vectors for Partial<T> (written `T~` in Ion source).
Consumed by all three in-repo runtimes; the three implementations must produce
byte-identical CBOR for the same patch.

wireFormat.container: CBOR map. Definite length on write; readers MUST also accept an indefinite-length map (0xBF ... 0xFF).
wireFormat.key: Text string holding the Ion field name.
wireFormat.value: CBOR null (0xF6) => the field is CLEARED; otherwise the field's ordinary Ion encoding => the field is MODIFIED.
wireFormat.absent: A field that does not appear in the map is UNTOUCHED.
wireFormat.order: Fields are written in Ion declaration order, so the same patch is byte-identical in every runtime.
wireFormat.removalEncoding: Removal is decided by the patch state, never by null-checking a stored value. `Modified(null)` and `Removed()` are the same three bytes; `null` in the map means CLEARED, and for a Maybe<T> field 'cleared' and 'set to none' are therefore the same patch.
wireFormat.migrationNote: roadmap 1.1 (explicit field indices) would let the key become an unsigned integer index instead of a name. Not implemented: the language has no field indices yet.

$floatEncoding: RESOLVED — see /tests/golden/float.golden.json for the full f2/f4/f8 vector set.
Every runtime now writes a float at its DECLARED width: f2 -> 0xF9 + 2 bytes,
f4 -> 0xFA + 4 bytes, f8 -> 0xFB + 8 bytes, always, regardless of value.
Previously System.Formats.Cbor's CborWriter.WriteSingle/WriteDouble shrank a float to the
shortest lossless CBOR float (1.5f -> 'f93e00', 4f -> 'f94400') in every conformance mode
except Ctap2Canonical, while packages/ion.webcore.js and packages/ion.rustcore (minicbor)
always emitted the declared width — so the three runtimes differed byte-wise on any f4/f8
value that happened to fit a smaller float. The vectors below originally used 1.1f to
sidestep that; 'modified-scalar-float-half-representable' now pins 1.5f, which is exactly
the case that used to diverge. src/ion.runtime/formatter.floats.cs forces the width with
CborWriter.WriteEncodedValue rather than switching conformance mode, because Ctap2Canonical
would also mandate sorted map keys and forbid indefinite lengths — which would break the
declaration-order map this file specifies under `wireFormat.order`.

message.name: GoldenPatchTarget
message.ion: msg GoldenPatchTarget { n: i4; f: f4; s: string; items: i4[]; note: string?; }

vectors.name: empty
vectors.notes: Empty patch: definite-length map with zero entries.

vectors.name: modified-scalar-float
vectors.notes: f4 value written as CBOR float32 (0xFA). 1.1f is not losslessly representable as float16, so this was the one float value all three runtimes already agreed on before the width rule landed — see $floatEncoding.

vectors.name: modified-scalar-float-half-representable
vectors.notes: R-FLOAT REGRESSION GUARD. 1.5f IS losslessly representable as float16, so this is precisely the case that used to diverge: C# wrote 'a16166f93e00' while TS and Rust wrote 'a16166fa3fc00000'. The declared f4 width must win. See $floatEncoding and /tests/golden/float.golden.json.

vectors.name: cleared-scalar-float
vectors.notes: R3 REGRESSION GUARD. Clearing a float MUST encode as null (0xF6). The old C# writer decided removal by null-checking the boxed value, so Removed() on a value-typed field wrote the field's default instead — 'a16166fa00000000' in every runtime today, and 'a16166f90000' in C# before the width rule landed — and removal silently became 'set to zero'.

vectors.name: modified-array
vectors.notes: A msg with an array field. R7 GUARD: the old C# formatter looked for a registered IonFormatter<IonArray<X>>, which never exists, and threw.

vectors.name: modified-optional-some
vectors.notes: A msg with an optional field, patched to Some.

vectors.name: modified-optional-none
vectors.notes: Deliberate aliasing (R4): 'modified to none' and 'cleared' are the same bytes and decode as 'cleared'. Encode-only, because the decode direction is covered by cleared-optional.

vectors.name: all-fields
vectors.notes: Every field touched. Entry order is Ion declaration order (n, f, s, items, note), NOT insertion order.

vectors.name: unknown-keys-skipped
vectors.notes: Decode-only. Map holds 'zzz': [1,2] and 'qq': null, neither of which is in the schema; both are skipped, including the null one.

vectors.name: indefinite-length-map
vectors.notes: Decode-only. R5 GUARD: an indefinite-length map (0xBF ... 0xFF). The old C# reader used length.GetValueOrDefault() and read zero entries, then desynchronised the reader on ReadEndMap(). Writers always emit definite length, so re-encoding produces 'a2616e076166f6'.
